accessibility.nonvisual_route: Every selected display includes ordered values or pairs and a feature narrative, while model cards state formulas, parameters, assumptions, fit checks, and revisions.

lessons.title: Report fit, limits, and predictions
learning_goals: Answer the modelling question with a claim whose scope and precision match the evidence.
Evaluate fit, uncertainty, assumptions, data quality, consequences, and limitations transparently.
Stress-test predictions across plausible scenarios and distinguish interpolation from unsupported extrapolation.
success_criteria: I link every conclusion to a calculation, distribution feature, point check, residual, or documented source fact.
I identify the most consequential assumption and explain how changing it could alter the decision.
I state valid domain, uncertainty and precision, affected groups, and a revision or next evidence step.

vocabulary.meaning: the degree and pattern of agreement between model results and observed evidence
the acknowledged range of doubt arising from data, measurement, sampling, assumptions, and future change
a specific boundary or weakness restricting how a result may be interpreted or used
a coherent set of input values and assumptions used to explore a possible outcome
the level of certainty and scope justified by the quality, fit, design, and amount of evidence

lessons.why_it_matters: A model only becomes useful when its result is communicated honestly enough for someone to act. Reporting fit, limits, uncertainty, and consequences protects readers from false precision and causal overreach, while scenarios show which conclusions remain stable when conditions change.

direct_instruction.heading: Build claim-evidence-limit chains
direct_instruction.body: Answer the exact question first, then cite the calculation or representation supporting the claim. Attach a limitation that constrains interpretation: sample coverage, measurement, missingness, model form, residuals, assumptions, time, place, or domain. Use wording such as suggests, estimates, or is associated when the design does not support stronger language.

direct_instruction.heading: Judge fit in context
direct_instruction.body: Report how fit was checked, including residual size and pattern, summary agreement, held-out points, or scenario performance. A small numerical error may still matter in a high-stakes decision, while a rough estimate may be adequate for early planning. State units and round to a precision supported by input measurement and model quality.

direct_instruction.heading: Stress-test predictions
direct_instruction.body: Calculate baseline, plausible low, and plausible high scenarios by changing consequential inputs or assumptions. Mark interpolation and extrapolation. Explain which decisions remain unchanged, which reverse, and what new evidence would reduce uncertainty. Include affected stakeholders and avoid presenting one scenario as an inevitable future.

method_routes.title: Claim-evidence-limitation report route
steps: Restate the modelling question and give a direct bounded answer.
Cite the strongest numerical and graphical evidence with source, units, and fit check.
State uncertainty, domain, sample or source limits, and assumptions beside the claim.
Identify affected stakeholders, possible consequence of error, and any causal boundary.
Recommend a decision, revision, or next evidence step proportional to the findings.
method_routes.when_useful: Use this route to turn a completed analysis into a concise report that a family, learner, educator, or decision maker can audit.
method_routes.check: Every major claim must have nearby evidence and a limitation, and no recommendation may exceed the model's validated purpose.

method_routes.title: Prediction stress-test route
steps: Define baseline inputs, assumptions, valid domain, and prediction precision.
Select one consequential uncertainty and set plausible low and high values from evidence.
Calculate outputs for all three scenarios using the same model.
Compare output range, decision threshold, sensitivity, and reversibility.
Classify prediction support and state what change would trigger revision or rejection.
method_routes.when_useful: Use this route when a recommendation depends on uncertain future inputs or an assumption whose change could reverse the decision.
method_routes.check: Scenario bounds must be plausible and sourced or clearly labelled, while extrapolation and unsupported futures remain explicit.

representations.label: Annotated model output
representations.description: A graph, table, or equation output carries claim labels, observed domain, fit evidence, uncertainty, assumption notes, and unsupported zones.
representations.text_alternative: Read question, bounded claim, model output, units, fit check, valid domain, uncertainty, assumptions, limitations, affected groups, and next step.

representations.label: Fit-limit-prediction table
representations.description: Rows connect baseline and stress scenarios to inputs, outputs, residual or fit evidence, claim strength, limitations, decisions, and revision triggers.
representations.text_alternative: For each scenario state inputs, assumptions, output, evidence, fit, prediction type, limitation, decision effect, and trigger for revision.

worked_examples.prompt: Report the fit of y = 2x for observed pairs (1,2), (2,4), (3,5), (4,8), (5,10).

steps.label: State evidence
steps.explanation: Residuals are 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, so four points fit exactly and one observed output is one below prediction.

steps.label: Bound the claim
steps.explanation: The model closely fits this small sample over x from 1 to 5, but source, context, measurement, and causal design are unspecified.

steps.label: Write report
steps.explanation: Use approximate association language, report the residual exception, and request new points before prediction outside the observed range.

worked_examples.answer: For these five pairs, y = 2x has close in-sample fit with maximum absolute residual 1; it supports approximate interpolation on 1 <= x <= 5 but not a causal or distant forecast claim.
worked_examples.verification: The report includes all residual evidence, observed domain, claim strength, and limits instead of reporting only the equation.

worked_examples.prompt: Stress-test profit P = 8n - 120 at n = 40 when net contribution may range from $6 to $9.

steps.label: Calculate scenarios
steps.explanation: At contributions $6, $8, and $9, profits are 120, 200, and 240 dollars for 40 items.

steps.label: Compare decision
steps.explanation: All scenarios remain positive, but the $120-to-$240 output range is large relative to the baseline.

steps.label: Report trigger
steps.explanation: Verify price and fee evidence; revise if contribution falls below $3 because then 40 items would not cover the $120 fixed cost.

worked_examples.answer: The positive-profit decision is stable across the stated $6-to-$9 scenarios, but expected profit is sensitive; verify contribution and use $3 per item as the break-even revision trigger at n = 40.
worked_examples.verification: Each scenario changes only contribution, calculations are shown, and the recommendation separates decision stability from output uncertainty.

misconceptions.claim: A limitation should be hidden because it weakens the report.
misconceptions.correction: A specific limitation makes the result usable by showing where it is reliable and where more evidence is needed.

misconceptions.claim: A model prediction is a promise about one future outcome.
misconceptions.correction: A prediction is conditional on inputs, assumptions, fit, and continuing relationships and should include uncertainty or scenarios.

misconceptions.claim: More decimal places make a claim more scientific.
misconceptions.correction: Precision must match measurement, data quality, model fit, and decision need; unsupported digits create false certainty.

guided.prompt: Which phrase best reports observational association?
guided.rationale: Association language matches observational paired evidence without asserting an untested causal mechanism.

guided.prompt: Observed inputs range from 5 to 20. Classify a prediction at input 12.
guided.rationale: Input twelve lies inside the observed interval, so the prediction is interpolation.

guided.prompt: Revise 'The model is perfect' using residuals 0, 1, -1, 0 and a domain 2 <= x <= 8.

response.sample_response: The model fits the four observed points closely on 2 <= x <= 8, with residuals between -1 and 1 and two exact matches. This supports approximate interpolation in that domain, not a claim of perfect or universal accuracy.

guided.rationale: The revision replaces absolute language with fit evidence, error size, domain, and bounded prediction strength.

independent.prompt: Which item belongs beside a model claim?
independent.rationale: Evidence supports the claim while a nearby limitation marks the boundary of responsible interpretation.

independent.prompt: A model uses data through 2025. Which claim needs new evidence?

options: the same relation will hold exactly in 2050
response.correct_answer: the same relation will hold exactly in 2050

independent.rationale: The distant future assertion extrapolates across time and assumes unchanged conditions without supporting evidence.

independent.prompt: Which output wording matches uncertain inputs measured to whole units?
independent.rationale: Approximate whole-unit wording better matches input precision and model uncertainty than unsupported decimals.

independent.prompt: What does a revision trigger state?

options: evidence or condition that prompts a model or decision change
response.correct_answer: evidence or condition that prompts a model or decision change

independent.rationale: A trigger makes monitoring actionable by defining when existing assumptions or recommendations no longer hold.

independent.prompt: Write a bounded report for a route whose observed median is 18 minutes, IQR is 5, range is 12 to 35, and n = 24 trips.

criteria: gives decision or next evidence step
response.sample_response: Across the 24 observed trips, the typical time was 18 minutes and the middle half spanned 5 minutes, while observed times ranged from 12 to 35. These sample conditions do not guarantee a future trip; a time-critical plan should add a buffer and collect more trips across relevant days and conditions.

independent.rationale: A responsible distribution report gives centre, spread, sample context, observed extremes, decision implication, and data limits.

retrieval.prompt: What prediction type extends beyond the observed input range?
retrieval.rationale: Extrapolation applies a model beyond the interval represented by the observed input data.

retrieval.prompt: Which evidence directly checks regression fit?
retrieval.rationale: Residuals quantify and reveal the structure of differences between observed and predicted outputs.

retrieval.prompt: Explain how a limitation differs from saying 'the model is bad.'

criteria: names a specific boundary or weakness
response.sample_response: A limitation identifies a specific issue, such as a small sample from one month, and explains that conclusions may not transfer to other seasons. This still allows use for the observed month and shows what new data would test broader use.

retrieval.rationale: Specific limitations guide responsible use and improvement, whereas a vague negative label provides no actionable boundary.

lessons.reflection_prompt: Which limitation or scenario most changed the strength of your final claim, and what evidence or threshold would trigger the next revision?

accessibility.nonvisual_route: Reports follow a fixed question-claim-evidence-fit-domain-uncertainty-assumption-limitation-consequence-prediction-revision sequence with all visuals restated.
response_options: spoken model briefing with an ordered evidence card

quiz.title: Unit 7 data analysis and modelling check

items.prompt: A service collects precise location every minute for a simple step-count feature. Identify one benefit, one risk, and one proportionality question.

criteria: asks whether less or coarser data could meet the purpose
response.sample_response: Frequent location could help map a route, but it exposes sensitive movement patterns if retained or reused. Ask whether on-device step totals or coarse, short-lived location would provide the feature with substantially less privacy risk.

items.rationale: A lifecycle analysis balances purpose and consequence and tests whether the data collected are necessary and proportionate.

items.prompt: For the ordered data 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, what is the median?
items.rationale: With six values, the median is the mean of the middle pair 5 and 7, which is 6.

items.prompt: A scatter plot shows a strong positive association between outdoor temperature and cold-drink sales. Explain why temperature may support prediction without proving it alone causes every sale.

response.sample_response: The variables move together, so temperature can help predict aggregate sales within the observed range. The plot alone cannot isolate cause because season, promotions, events, and customer traffic may also affect sales, and it cannot determine each person's choice.

items.rationale: Regression describes association in observed data, while a causal claim requires design and evidence that address alternative explanations.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes a mathematical model?

options: an answer that needs no evidence

items.rationale: A useful model keeps selected relationships for a purpose and necessarily leaves some real-world detail outside its boundary.

items.prompt: Which question is most modelable with a small public data set?

options: How did daily temperature relate to public electricity demand in Toronto during July 2025?
response.correct_answer: How did daily temperature relate to public electricity demand in Toronto during July 2025?

items.rationale: The selected question names variables, place, timeframe, and an association that can be investigated with bounded public data.

items.prompt: Design the privacy boundary for a five-day study of homework duration without collecting student identities.

criteria: includes adult approval or public-data alternative
response.sample_response: Each learner may record only their own rounded daily minutes using an unlinked code, with no name, account, contact, health, or location data. State the study purpose, keep data locally for the five-day analysis, delete raw records afterward, and use an adult-approved public sample instead if participation is not freely chosen.

items.rationale: A low-risk plan minimizes data, separates identity, limits use and retention, and provides a non-participation alternative.

items.prompt: Which display best compares the distribution of one numerical variable across two groups?
items.rationale: Aligned box plots show median, middle spread, and overall spread for both groups on a common numerical scale.

items.prompt: Which revision makes the claim 'the model predicts exactly forever' defensible?

options: the model gives approximate predictions within the observed range under stated assumptions
response.correct_answer: the model gives approximate predictions within the observed range under stated assumptions

items.rationale: A defensible report matches precision to fit, bounds prediction to evidence, and makes its assumptions visible.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts a box plot and a scatter plot?

options: a box plot summarizes one-variable distribution; a scatter plot shows paired-variable association
a box plot requires paired coordinates
a scatter plot only shows a median
response.correct_answer: a box plot summarizes one-variable distribution; a scatter plot shows paired-variable association

items.rationale: The displays answer different questions: distribution of one variable versus association between two paired variables.

items.prompt: Outline a complete modelling cycle for a question about a bounded public data set, including a point where the model might be revised.

criteria: uses evidence to revise question data or model
response.sample_response: Ask a focused question with variables, population, and timeframe; audit a documented public source; clean and display the data; compare candidate models against points or residuals; answer the question with fit, limits, and bounded predictions; then revise the question, data plan, or model if patterns, outliers, or assumptions conflict with the evidence.

items.rationale: Modelling is an iterative question-data-model-report process rather than a single calculation or decorative graph.

performance_task.title: Low-risk mathematical modelling investigation
performance_task.prompt: Complete an adult-approved modelling investigation using a reviewed public data set or a deliberately low-risk, voluntary, minimized collection that contains no direct identifiers or sensitive personal information. Ask a focused question, document the data lifecycle and affected stakeholders, audit source quality and privacy, choose suitable one- or two-variable displays, compare candidate analyses or models, and answer the question. Report fit, uncertainty, assumptions, consequential limitations, interpolation or extrapolation boundaries, and at least one justified revision. Include a full paper-readable data sample and ordered text alternatives; a local spreadsheet or graphing tool may calculate or check results, but an AI tutor, cloud account, public posting, or undisclosed personal-data collection is not required or permitted.
required_components: a focused question naming variables, population or system, timeframe, decision purpose, and feasible scope
an adult-approved source and data-lifecycle map covering collection, storage, processing, representation, use, retention, and affected groups
a privacy and ethics boundary that minimizes data, avoids sensitive identifiers, documents consent where applicable, and offers a reviewed public-data route
source metadata, assumptions, changing and controlled factors, quality limitations, cleaning decisions, and a reproducible data sample
an appropriate one-variable or paired-variable display with scale, units, ordered text alternative, and calculations
at least two candidate summaries or models compared with point checks, distribution evidence, or residuals
a claim answering the original question with evidence, fit judgment, precision, and valid-domain limits
a benefit-risk-consequence analysis and a prediction stress test across at least two plausible scenarios
one evidence-driven revision to the question, data plan, representation, model, or final claim

rubric.criteria: The question is feasible and unbiased, while source, consent, minimization, privacy, affected groups, and retention are handled transparently and safely.
Calculations, displays, scales, units, quartile convention or paired-variable structure, and text alternatives fit the data and question.
Candidate approaches are compared with evidence, fit is checked using data or residuals, and an evidence-driven revision is documented.
Claims answer the question without causal overreach, match the model's precision, and restrict predictions to justified scenarios and domains.
Source metadata, assumptions, methods, sample data, consequences, limitations, and reasoning are complete enough to reproduce without AI or cloud access.
